findings.summary: WIF/STS failures are logged without their AWS or Anthropic request ID. log_failure reads request_id from the outer TokenUnavailable, which has no request ID, so it logs request_id=nil. This goes against D2.4 and D5.2.
findings.scenario: STS returns AccessDenied (400) to the warmer. The refresher logs 'Claude WIF token refresh failed (Aws::STS::Errors::AccessDenied: ...)' with no x-amzn-requestid. The next translation raises TokenUnavailable with that error as its cause. The mapper classifies the cause as SERVICE_MISCONFIGURED, but log_failure takes request_id from the outer TokenUnavailable and logs request_id=nil. A WorkloadIdentityError#request_id from the token endpoint is also never logged. The operator has no ID to look up in CloudTrail or give Anthropic support, and this change now surfaces these failures at error level. Unverified: whether the mapper really reads the cause and the log line reads the outer error depends on the finder's reading.
findings.fix: When the error is a TokenUnavailable, have log_failure take the request ID from its cause: WorkloadIdentityError#request_id, or the x-amzn-requestid header from context.http_response.headers for an Aws::Errors::ServiceError. Add the same ID to the refresher's 'refresh failed' log line.
findings.lenses: area:STS identity token robustness and error classification

findings.summary: During a persistent-401 backoff, await_token(after: nil) returns the rejected token before it checks @backing_off, so requests do not fail fast. Each one pays a Claude round trip and gets a 401.
findings.scenario: Claude rejects forced gen 2. wait_until_due returns :rejected and sets @backing_off, and the warmer sleeps for up to 60 s. Every new translation in that window calls await_token(after: nil), and line 110 (`usable? && after.nil?`) hands back gen 2 before line 111 checks @backing_off. The SDK sends gen 2, Claude answers 401, and the translator logs a warn and retries with after: 2, which raises TokenRejected. So each request costs an extra round trip and a warn log, and Anthropic receives a known-bad bearer each time. The requests still fail correctly. The rewritten comment and D5.2 say requests fail fast.
findings.fix: Record the rejected generation in the :rejected branch, and make await_token fail at once while backing off and @generation <= that value. If one 401 round trip per request is acceptable, change the comment and D5.2 to say so instead.
findings.lenses: area:Token refresher warmer backoff and short-lived token rejection

findings.summary: The test's `@next_force == false` assertion can no longer fail, because nothing in the app sets TokenCache@next_force after this change. The test does not check the refresher's pending state.
findings.scenario: 4993a9c removed the translator's only call to token_cache.invalidate. The SDK's own invalidate runs only when max_retries > 0, and ClientFactory builds the client with max_retries: 0. The assertion therefore holds whatever the refresher does. The only real check left is the exchange count (times: 2). The refresher's @refresh_after and @backing_off, which the test name now refers to, are never checked.
findings.fix: Drop the @next_force assertion, or replace it with a check on the refresher's state. That could be seconds_until_refresh, or a third request that proves no extra exchange happens.
findings.lenses: area:Charging a 401 to the right token and retrying once

result.note: No merges: the three findings are separate defects (a logging gap, the backoff fast-fail ordering, and a vacuous test assertion). The must-fix set is empty, because none of these is worth holding the merge for. The worst is a missing request ID in failure logs, which hurts diagnosis but not correctness. The backoff finding leaves requests failing correctly, only one round trip late. No findings moved between scopes. The pre-existing finding says log_failure and the refresher's log line are unchanged in 864dcad...mvp. The two introduced findings name the commit or comment rewrite that introduced them. Severities are kept as filed. All three findings are unverified.
